findings.title: Privacy notice treats simply browsing as consent
findings.detail: The privacy notice says that proceeding with a visit constitutes acceptance and consent. The fresh audit found no cookie banner and no successful reject action, so this does not provide a clear affirmative consent mechanism before any non-essential storage or access.
findings.law: PECR reg. 6; UK GDPR Articles 4(11), 7 and 5(1)(a)
findings.policy_quote: By providing your personal information as described above, or by proceeding with your visit to QinetiQ’s websites, you are accepting and consenting to the practices described in this Privacy Notice, and you agree to the transfer, storing or processing of your personal information in the manner described in this Notice.
findings.reasoning: Mere browsing is not normally unambiguous consent under UK GDPR, and PECR requires prior consent for non-essential device storage or access. This is medium rather than high because the evidence does not show the contents of network requests or prove that non-essential tracking actually occurred.
findings.law_eu: ePrivacy Directive 2002/58/EC Art. 5(3) (consent before storing/reading on a device); EU GDPR Articles 4(11), 7 and 5(1)(a)

findings.title: Observed experience contradicts the cookie policy's promised choices
findings.detail: The cookie policy says that visitors will be shown a message with Accept all, Reject and Manage preferences options. The audit found no banner and no successful reject action, which may prevent users from making the promised simple choice.
findings.law: PECR reg. 6; UK GDPR Articles 5(1)(a) and 7
findings.policy_quote: Upon accessing our website a message will be shown with a link to the cookie policy (this page) and three options:
findings.reasoning: If the observed behaviour is accurate, the site's stated consent and rejection process was not available and the policy was not transparent about the actual experience. Medium severity is appropriate because the automated check may have failed to detect an interface element, and no actual tracking request was provided.
findings.law_eu: ePrivacy Directive 2002/58/EC Art. 5(3) (consent before storing/reading on a device); EU GDPR Articles 5(1)(a) and 7

findings.title: Accept is one click, but we found no way to reject
findings.detail: The banner offers "Cookie policy", but our automated check could not find any reject or decline option. (This may be a limit of our check, so treat it as something to verify.)
findings.law: ICO cookie guidance (refusing must be as easy as accepting)
findings.law_eu: EDPB Guidelines 05/2020 on consent; EDPB Cookie Banner Taskforce report (2023)

ai_review.summary: The main concern is that the privacy notice treats continuing to browse as consent, which is not a reliable substitute for prior, affirmative consent under PECR and UK GDPR. The audit also conflicts with the cookie policy's promise of Accept, Reject and Manage preferences options. The evidence does not show request contents or prove that non-essential cookies or trackers were set, so the findings are assessed as medium rather than high.
evidence: E1: Cookie banner found: False. Reject clicked successfully: False. Method: failed. Buttons clicked: none.
E2: Privacy policy: https://www.qinetiq.com/en/privacy-notice. Companies it names: none extracted. Contact email found: DPOFFICE@QinetiQ.com.
